title: Kenyan Crème Caramel
community: Urban Kenya — the classic hotel buffet dessert
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Kenyan Crème Caramel — silky, wobbly custard baked in a caramel-lined mould and unmoulded to reveal a gleaming caramel topping. The hotel buffet dessert that never loses its elegance — simple ingredients, classical technique, extraordinary result.
longDesc: Crème caramel has been on the menu of every Nairobi hotel since the first French-trained chefs arrived. It never goes out of style because it is genuinely perfect — the wobbling custard, the caramel that flows over the plate, the contrast of sweet and slightly bitter caramel with the creamy egg custard.
steps: Make caramel: heat sugar and water without stirring until deep amber. Pour quickly into ramekins, tilting to coat base. Work fast.
Make custard: whisk eggs, yolks, and sugar. Heat milk and cream until just steaming. Pour slowly over egg mixture, whisking. Add vanilla. Strain.
Place ramekins in a roasting tin. Fill with boiling water halfway up the ramekins.
Bake at 160°C for 35—40 minutes until set with a slight wobble in the centre.
Cool completely. Refrigerate at least 4 hours.
To serve: run a knife around the edge. Place a plate on top. Invert firmly.
chefTips: The caramel must be deep amber — pale caramel is too sweet; very dark adds desirable bitterness.
The bain-marie keeps oven temperature gentle — direct heat produces curdled custard.
It must wobble when baked — a fully set crème caramel is over-baked.
cookingScience: Egg proteins coagulate between 60—85°C. The bain-marie limits the maximum temperature the custard reaches to just under 100°C — far enough above 85°C to set the custard but gentle enough to prevent the rapid coagulation that creates a rubbery, curdled texture. The caramel provides invertase-converted sugars that flow when the dessert is inverted, creating the sauce.
sustainabilityTips: Local Kenyan eggs and milk make this entirely locally sourced.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days before unmoulding.
reheating: Serve cold or at room temperature.
culturalNote: Crème caramel is one of the most enduring desserts on Kenya's hotel menus — a French classic that has been served in Nairobi for generations and continues to be ordered with the same pleasure.
